title: Weather Watch

beats.narrativeText: The expedition's weather station flickers back to partial life. It's been recording nothing for years — Atlas asks the learner to be the one who restarts it.

The station kept detailed weather records once, and stopped for a reason nobody has explained yet. Comparing today's weather with those archives might be the only way to find out why it mattered enough to track so carefully.
The learner records today's observations and measures — or carefully estimates — the temperature.
Turning today's readings into simple charts makes something visible that raw numbers alone didn't: today's weather sitting right alongside the expedition's own historical data.
The learner must look across old and new data together and identify whatever pattern is emerging — not just what today looks like, but what today has in common with the past.
The pattern isn't just about weather anymore — it starts to explain choices the expedition made long before the learner ever arrived.
The learner reflects on how something as ordinary as today's weather turned out to connect directly to decisions made years ago.
The learner's readings are added to the expedition archive — no longer just today's weather, but part of a record that's clearly still being written.

activities.title: Record Observations
activities.storyContext: The weather station has been silent for years and only just started working again — today's observations are the first new entry in a very old record.
activities.instructions: Record today's weather conditions — sky, wind and any other details you notice — as if this entry might matter to someone reading it years from now.
activities.output: A weather observation entry in the Explorer Journal.

activities.title: Measure Temperature
activities.storyContext: An accurate reading today is the only way to fairly compare against the expedition's own archived records.
activities.instructions: Measure today's temperature if a thermometer is available. If not, estimate it as carefully as you can, and note that it's an estimate.
activities.output: A recorded or estimated temperature reading.

activities.title: Create Simple Charts
activities.storyContext: Numbers on a page are easy to miss a pattern in — a chart makes today's weather easy to line up against the expedition's own records.
activities.instructions: Create a simple chart to record your weather observations, laid out so it's easy to compare against the archived data.

activities.title: Compare Historical and Current Data
activities.storyContext: Somewhere in the comparison between old and new is a pattern that may explain choices the expedition made long ago.
activities.instructions: Compare today's chart with the expedition's archived weather records, and note anything that repeats or stands out.
activities.output: Notes on how today's weather compares with the archived records.

activities.title: Predict Tomorrow's Weather
activities.storyContext: Explorers use evidence to make predictions, not guesses.
activities.instructions: Use your collected evidence to predict what tomorrow's weather will be like, and explain your reasoning.
activities.output: A weather prediction with supporting reasoning.

activities.title: How Meteorologists Make Forecasts
activities.storyContext: Predicting weather is a real scientific discipline.
activities.instructions: Find out how meteorologists make weather forecasts.
activities.output: None required — this is an open investigation.

prompts: What pattern did you notice when comparing today's weather with the archived records, and what might it explain about the expedition's decisions?

discussionPoints: What pattern did you notice in the weather data?
Why might weather have affected the expedition's decisions?
parentGuide.preparation: A thermometer is useful if available, but estimating is acceptable.
parentGuide.assessment: Look for accurately recorded observations and a chart that makes a pattern easy to see.

completionCriteria: Weather observations recorded, charts created, and historical data compared with current data.
